title: Harnessing natural RNA triplex elements found in lncRNAs MALAT1 and NEAT1 for engineering of novel riboswitch platforms.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the whole open-access full text and the machine-readable article XML. The XML lists exactly one supplementary item, a 948 KB Word document (gkag747_supplemental_file.docx); there is no deposited dataset, no accession of any kind (Europe PMC text-mined accessions empty, no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI). I tried to download the Word file three ways: the PMC /bin/ path returned a 1,817-byte challenge page, the Europe PMC fulltextRepo endpoint returned HTTP 500, and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out. I counted the named constructs in the text myself: about 25-30 distinct plasmids (MALAT1, MALAT1_in, Tet_9/7/5/3, Tet_7.1-7.7 series, Tet_7.7_Arich, Tet_7.7_noA, Tet_7.2_masc, Tet_7.2_degron, NEAT1_Tet_7/7.3/8/9, TetK19, TetK19A42G and a few reporter swaps).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That Supplementary Table S1 contains 'sequences used' (methods text), and the measured values themselves: fold inductions of 2.0, 4.1, 17.8, 20.5, 25 and 42 and relative luciferase activities such as 300.0 +/- 39.1% and 9.3%, all of which appear in figure captions and running text as bar-chart values, not as a table I could open.

a1_downloadable.note: Open access, no login or application. But the only data object is one Word document; I could not actually retrieve it (PMC challenge page, Europe PMC 500 and timeout), so nothing was opened.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The thing a model would predict - tetracycline-induced fold change in reporter expression - exists only as bars in Figures 2-7 and numbers in the text. Supplementary Table S1 is described as a list of sequences; no table of measured values is provided anywhere, so the label would have to be transcribed from figures by hand.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences are reportedly all in Supplementary Table S1 (paper text only; file not retrievable), so inputs would likely be present if the file opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clear in the captions: Renilla luciferase normalised to firefly luciferase on the same vector, expressed as percent of the parental psiCHECK-2 vector, plus fold induction with/without 50 micromolar tetracycline.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. About 25-30 individually cloned constructs, each measured in three to four biological replicates. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification. This is roughly fifty times too small; it is a low-throughput, one-construct-at-a-time study, not a library screen.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small - a few dozen short RNA sequences and their reporter readouts.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not properly checkable: no data file opened. The construct count I derived from the text is consistent with the figures described, but there is no file to compare it against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label provenance is clean in principle: a physical dual-luciferase assay in HeLa/HEK293 cells, not another model's output and not computed from the sequence features.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) would be the obvious backbone for riboswitch sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU only; the dataset is a few dozen short sequences
backbone.licence: not checked - stopped at Part A

integration.join_key: none - the constructs are synthetic designs with no standard identifier
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: there is no identifier in this paper's data that joins it to a large public resource.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the known destabilising A-rich-tract mutant (MALAT1_in), which drops expression 32-fold and any working model must rank as low-expressing.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable in principle but meaningless at n~30.
controls.external_validation: Published tetracycline-aptamer riboswitch and aptazyme datasets from the same field exist, but none was verified here and none shares this triplex architecture.

honest_claim_h3: With ~30 hand-cloned constructs whose readouts exist only in figures, no model trained on this paper could claim more than 'it memorised a few dozen rationally designed communication-module variants from one lab, one ligand and one reporter'.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a synthetic riboswitch's RNA sequence to predict how much a drug switches the gene it controls on.
plain_idea.train_on: The RNA sequence of each engineered switch (a stabilising triple-helix element from the long non-coding RNAs MALAT1 or NEAT1, a tetracycline-binding aptamer, and the short 'communication module' linking them). Only about 25-30 such constructs exist in this paper.
plain_idea.predict: The fold change in reporter protein output when the antibiotic tetracycline is added, measured by a dual-luciferase assay in human cells (Renilla luciferase signal normalised to firefly luciferase on the same plasmid, three to four biological replicates).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building drug-controllable RNA therapeutics would like to pick a linker sequence computationally instead of cloning and testing them one at a time; but that needs thousands of measured variants, which this paper does not have.

ml_idea: Considered: predict tetracycline-dependent fold induction from riboswitch sequence (triple-helix element plus aptamer plus communication module), using a frozen RNA language model such as RNA-FM with a small regression head. Dead on arrival here because the paper provides only ~30 constructs and no table of measured values.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: a few dozen sequences under ~200 nucleotides each. The eight hours is hand-transcribing bar-chart values from figures and typing sequences out of a Word document, not computation.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the constructs with a measured fold induction. I did this from the full text: about 25-30, versus the ~400 minimum. That single count kills it, and no download was needed.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2: only about 25-30 hand-cloned constructs, and their measured fold-induction values exist only as bars in figures - no table of labels is deposited anywhere. This is an elegant low-throughput synthetic biology paper (a new triple-helix-based riboswitch platform reaching 42-fold induction), but there is no feature/label table and no path to one. The same idea would be worth revisiting on a paper that reports a pooled library of thousands of communication-module variants with sequencing-based readouts.
